title: How Ronald Araujo Rediscovered His Best Form After Barcelona Exit
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Andrew Headspeath4:00 PM EDTRonald Araújo is a hit. /  Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty ImagesLiverpool and loan signings have not paired well in recent years.

There was Steven Caulker, the big center back thrown on as an auxiliary striker while Jürgen Klopp made kitchen sink signals from the touchline. Ozan Kabak, the injury crisis band-aid who was only marginally better than having no defenders at all. And who can forget all 13 cursed minutes of Arthur Melo’s temporary switch?

As a result of these signings’ performances, and several others, hopes were not especially high when Liverpool announced the arrival of Ronald Araújo on a season-long deal with an option to buy back in August.

Yes, the Uruguayan arrived as the Barcelona captain, but he had started only 11 La Liga matches in 2025–26. Once rated as one of the best defenders in Spanish soccer, question marks over his rashness, positional lapses and injury record had since turned into honking great exclamation points. General consensus was that Liverpool, unmoored by the dual exits of FSG’s CEO of Football Michael Edwards and sporting director Richard Hughes, had panic bought their defensive cover.
Less than three months on, Araújo has a very strong case to be considered as Liverpool’s player of the season so far.

Signed in part for his versatility, the 27-year-old has excelled at both right back and in the center of defense, starting six out of eight games in the Premier League so far, winning praise by the boat-load for his commitment and ferocity.

While defensive signings to the Premier League from La Liga are often critiqued for their perceived reluctance to get stuck in, Araújo plays like he was raised on Pure Barclays. It is his love of blood and thunder defending that has endeared him to the Anfield crowd and social media has been awash with love for “Big Ron” in the early months of this season.

In Sunday’s 2–0 win over Brighton, the defender was awarded Player of the Match after putting in a shift that included a rarely-seen sliding header tackle inside his own box to preserve the Reds’ clean sheet. He also won all five of his duels in that match, made 11 defensive contributions and recorded a top speed of 36.3 km/h—supposedly the fastest clocked in the Premier League this season so far.

It is not just at the back Araújo is excelling. The Reds’ new No. 33 already has two Champions League goals and an assist—the latter a delightful backheel to set up Dominik Szoboszlai in the comeback win over Atlético Madrid.

In that same outing, Araújo sprinted upwards of 70 yards—simply for the love of the press—forcing Jan Oblak to hoof it long. It was a moment reminiscent of Andy Robertson’s famous lung-busting run against Manchester City all those years ago that secured the Scotsman as a bonafide fan-favorite.
Viral moments help calcify a player’s reputation at a new club. There have been plenty of them for Araújo already, who is becoming Liverpool’s one-man meme machine.

Araújo’s short spell has been rife with viral moments. / Liverpool FC/ Getty ImagesAraújo’s find-a-man-who-does-it-all displays have been incredibly welcome in a Liverpool team in danger of slipping towards mediocrity during a transition period, helping provide a dynamism that has often been lacking.
But his arrival has also proven exactly the sort of fresh start Araújo found himself needing, half a year on from his leave of absence from Barcelona for mental health reasons.

Araújo has spoken positively of Barcelona’s support for him while dealing with his anxiety struggles, but sometimes a change of scenery is just what’s needed. With Liverpool, it appears to be a perfect match of player and environment.
“The fans have absolutely fallen in love with him straight away,” Jamie Carragher said of Araújo last month.

“Sometimes you have players like that. They’ve come, they’ve got a bit of a backstory. At Barcelona maybe they were happy to see him go, but the Liverpool supporters opened their arms and gave him a big cuddle, and he seems to be enjoying it.”

On the pitch, he is already diving into the crowd and kissing the badge. Off it, the defender is said to have embraced life on Merseyside, and he has multiple Spanish speakers supporting him in the Liverpool locker room.

Araújo lifted the La Liga title as Barcelona captain last season. / Eric Alonso/Getty ImagesAs it stands, Liverpool have a £47 million ($63 million) option to buy Araújo at the end of the season. On current form, it may seem like a no-brainer, but there are reasons why this love affair could end up being only a fling.
